summary: Unexpected 5xx elevation during concurrent model-variant eviction and prefetch cancellation
description:
Issue summary: Customers started reporting a sharp increase in 5xx responses (~20x baseline) for embedding and chat routes between 14:12-14:38 UTC. Elevation correlated with a tenant (LexiSearch dedicated pool) performing concurrent requests that triggered model-variant eviction and a series of prefetch cancellations. Impact: LexiSearch experienced degraded throughput and 10+ minute retries; several streaming sessions dropped. Environment: prod (us-east), dedicated pool assigned to customer. Observed at multiple edge nodes in us-east; no config rollout at the time.

Observed behavior: api-gateway returned 502/503s intermittently, with serving-runtime upstream showing SIGABRT and runtime restarts. Accept-queue length spiked concurrently and keepalive reuse dropped. Prefetch subsystem logged repeated cancellation events with simultaneous eviction of variant shards; KV-cache saw hot-shard lock contention.

Why this ticket: Customer-facing incident requires triage + immediate mitigation (reduce customer impact) and post-incident action (fix eviction-prefetch interaction).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use a dedicated tenant with mixed embedding + chat workload.
2) Send concurrent high-rate embedding uploads (parallel multipart batches) while also running medium-sized chat bursts pinned to a model variant.
3) Trigger model-variant eviction by repeatedly toggling a model pin/rollout on the tenant and concurrently canceling several in-flight prefetch requests.
4) Observe accept-queue growth and increased 5xx responses at api-gateway.

Notes: reproduction requires dedicated pool isolation and may be rate-sensitive; seen reproducible in controlled perf lab with scaled-down traffic profile (50% of customer traffic) after ~5 minutes.
logs:
Sample lines from runtime logs: 
[2026-03-12T14:17:03Z] serving-runtime(worker-23) ERROR: eviction: variant shard 0x7f evicted while prefetch active
[2026-03-12T14:17:03Z] prefetch INFO: cancelling prefetch request id=pf_9c1a; reason=eviction-in-progress
[2026-03-12T14:17:04Z] api-gateway WARN: accept_queue_length=842 target=200; enqueue_latency_ms=312
[2026-03-12T14:17:05Z] serving-runtime(worker-23) FATAL: signal SIGABRT at 0x0000; backtrace: ... ; restarting runtime
[2026-03-12T14:17:05Z] api-gateway ERROR: upstream reset while reading response; returning 502 to client

Attached traces: grafana panels show apigw 5xx rate rising at 14:12 and CPU on runtime worker threads spiking immediately before SIGABRTs.

investigation_notes: Timeline: spike began at ~14:12 UTC; initial mitigation (scale up) temporarily reduced accept-queue but didn't prevent subsequent runtime restarts. Root cause hypothesis evolved: not pure load but an interactive race between eviction and prefetch cancellation creating a dangling pointer leading to SIGABRT. Evidence: repeating stack traces tied to kv-cache write path while eviction is logged within same millisecond window. Observed hot shards: shard_id set 0 and 3 had >90% of eviction events. Accept-queue behavior: long tail of enqueue latency grew until runtime restarted; api-gateway then returned 502/503s. Reproducible in perf lab when interleaving variant rollouts with heavy embedding prefetch cancellation. Related to prior issue SUP-472901 (connection thrashing) but distinct root cause. Action items created: 1) patch eviction/prefetch synchronization (PR linked), 2) add guardrails to prevent eviction when prefetch active for tenant-heavy shards, 3) improve metrics to alert earlier (prefetch_cancel_rate + shard_eviction_rate correlation), 4) run a canary rollout and validate with LexiSearch traffic patterns.
resolution: Workaround applied: instructed customer to reduce embedding multipart concurrency and applied temporary per-tenant prefetch rate cap; scaled dedicated pool + rolling restarts cleared transient fragmentation. Engineering produced hotfix PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/5821) that introduces a mutex around eviction callback + safe-cancel checks. Planned rollout: canary in prod us-east (5% traffic) 2026-03-13 18:00 UTC, followed by fast-fail rollback window. Postmortem actions: add runbook steps to throttle prefetch on eviction spikes, instrument KV-lock hold times, and schedule post-deploy verification with LexiSearch.
